hints: Focus on what type of reaction can happen here, a more reactive halogen displacing a less reactive halide ion.
Recall the reactivity order $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$, so only a halogen above can oxidise the halide below it.
Check which pair gives X able to oxidise Z but not Y, while Z is too weak to oxidise Y.
walkthrough:
**Spot the chemistry involved**

All the choices involve halogens ($\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$, $\text{I}_2$) and hydrogen halides ($\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$, $\text{HI}$). This is about halogen displacement.

Remember the rule:
$$\text{more reactive halogen + less reactive halide} \rightarrow \text{reaction}$$

**Recall the reactivity order**

Reactivity decreases down Group 17. Chlorine is the strongest oxidising agent here, then bromine, then iodine.
$$\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$$
So $\text{Cl}_2$ can displace $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$, $\text{Br}_2$ can only displace $\text{I}^-$, and $\text{I}_2$ displaces nothing.

**Apply the three observations**

X + Z reacts, so X must be a halogen above Z. X + Y shows no reaction, and Z + Y shows no reaction.

Only $\text{X} = \text{Cl}_2(aq)$, $\text{Y} = \text{I}_2(aq)$, $\text{Z} = \text{HBr}(aq)$ fits: $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{HBr} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + \text{Br}_2$ reacts, while $\text{Cl}_2$ with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{HBr}$ with $\text{I}_2$ do not react.

options.A: X = $\text{Br}_2$ and Z = $\text{HBr}$ contains $\text{Br}^-$. Bromine cannot oxidise its own halide ion, so X + Z would show no reaction. The question requires an immediate reaction for X + Z.
options.B: X = $\text{Cl}_2$ is more reactive than both $\text{Br}^-$ in Z and $\text{I}_2$ in Y. $\text{Cl}_2$ with $\text{I}_2$ gives no reaction. $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{HBr} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + \text{Br}_2$ gives the observed immediate reaction. $\text{HBr}$ with $\text{I}_2$ gives no reaction because $\text{Br}_2$ is more reactive than $\text{I}_2$. All three observations match.
options.C: Here Z = $\text{Br}_2$ and Y = $\text{HI}$ contains $\text{I}^-$. Since bromine is more reactive than iodine, $\text{Br}_2 + 2\text{HI} \rightarrow 2\text{HBr} + \text{I}_2$ would react. The question states Z + Y shows no reaction, so this fails. Also X + Z ($\text{HCl}$ + $\text{Br}_2$) would not react.
options.D: X = $\text{HCl}$ and Z = $\text{HBr}$ are both halides with no elemental halogen to act as oxidiser. Mixing them gives no reaction, but the question requires X + Z to react immediately. Students choosing this forget that two halide ions alone cannot undergo displacement.
